cba_marker: Standard veteran extension window open since July 8, 2026, the third anniversary of the July 8, 2023 rookie scale extension (5- or 6-season contracts extend after the third anniversary, Art. VII Sec. 7(a)(1)); reported at two years, about $122 million. The supermax (Designated Veteran) window is closed this summer: the 61-game 2025-26 fell short of the 65 games All-NBA requires (Art. XXIX Sec. 6).

July 2027: Designated Veteran Player Extension window opens (seven Years of Service, one or two seasons left, drafted by the team, Art. II Sec. 7(c)(ii)) IF he is All-NBA in 2026-27, which needs 65 games; six seasons from signing (Art. I Sec. 1(r)), so two remaining plus four new, the reported four-year deal.

Walk year. July 2028: the last extension window before free agency; the Designated Veteran version needs All-NBA in 2027-28 (the two-of-three route is closed by the 2025-26 miss). Contract ends June 30, 2029; unrestricted free agent July 2029.
Model assumption from Part 1: a star who survives his walk year re-signs on a fresh four-year deal, so the clock restarts.
Fresh deal's own cliff approaches; the hazard climbs back.
